item.title: US will stop $4b funding to Israel at end of 2026: Trump
item.description:
ISRAEL-PALESTINIANS-TRUMP-NETANYAHU

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year.

Speaking to Fox News' Fox and Friends, Trump said Israel no longer needed the funding and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using the US financial support to Israel as a talking point to criticize Republicans.

"Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping," Trump told Fox News' Fox and Friends.

"We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it," he said.

There was no immediate comment from Netanyahu's office on Trump's remarks.

It was not immediately clear which exact funding Trump meant. A memorandum of understanding that provides $3.8 billion annual US military aid to Israel is approaching its expiration date in 2028 and conversations have been under way on how Washington's assistance to Israel would evolve beyond that date.

"They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world," Trump added on Tuesday.

Netanyahu said in a May interview with CBS that he hoped to wean Israel off US military support within a decade. In a June letter to a US congressman he wrote that the time had come for Israel "to move from aid recipient to partner."

US public support for Israel has fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats. A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48 per cent of voters and 66 per cent of Democrats believe the United States is too supportive of Israel, up from 16 per cent and 20 per cent when the question was first asked in 2017.

Support for Israel among Democratic voters has plummeted, candidates critical of Israel are winning Democratic primaries and even moderate lawmakers are increasingly willing to challenge decades of US support for Israel.

"The left uses the $4 billion payment that everybody knows about, well it's no secret, as a signal of unfairness, and we can't allow that to happen," Trump said.

"We were giving them 4 billion, we are, but it gets cut off at the end of the year," he said. "Why? Because they don't need it."

item.title: ‘I am a poor man’s son, I could not resist the temptation of money’: ‘Coordinator’ Riyad
item.description:
First, they raided the house of former member of parliament (MP) Shammi Ahmed with the police. After failing to find her, the police left. But the men returned to the house shortly afterwards and threatened to have her husband arrested, branding him an ‘Awami League collaborator’. They demanded Tk 5 million in extortion money, of which the self-proclaimed ‘coordinators’ managed to collect Tk 1 million. A few days later, five of them were caught by police when they returned to collect the remaining Tk 4 million. Another suspect was arrested subsequently.

The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has submitted a charge sheet against six people before the court after completing its investigation into the case filed over the incident in Gulshan.

According to the PBI investigation, following the political changeover on 5 August, the accused began identifying themselves as coordinators and active members of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement. Taking advantage of this identity, they regularly visited police stations and developed close ties with police officers by offering assistance in arresting leaders and activists affiliated with the Awami League who were accused in various cases, as well as providing information about their whereabouts.

The investigation found that the accused subsequently used this access to evade the attention of law enforcement agencies and identify various individuals as Awami League collaborators, associates or supporters. They allegedly demanded and collected money by threatening them with cases, arrest and harassment. Through these activities, the accused exploited their influence for personal gain and obtained illegal financial benefits.

In the charge sheet, investigating officer Firoz Ahmed Munshi stated that the investigation and evidence had established the offences under Sections 143, 448, 385 and 386 of the Penal Code against Abdur Razzak alias Riyad and Jane Alam Apu. Meanwhile, preliminary evidence had established offences under Sections 143, 448 and 385 against the other accused, Sakadoun Siam, Sadman Sadab and Ibrahim Hossain.

The case was filed at Gulshan Police Station on 27 July 2025 by Siddiq Abu Zafar, 75. He lives in a house on Road 83 in Gulshan-2. According to the investigation records, his wife is former MP Shammi Ahmed.

Initially, Sub-Inspector (SI) Mokhlesur Rahman of Gulshan Police Station investigated the case. The PBI subsequently took over the investigation. Its SI Firoz Ahmed Munshi submitted the charge sheet against six people on 15 October after completing the investigation.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, he said, “As one of the accused is a minor, he will be tried in the juvenile court. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for 10 November. The court will hear arguments on whether to accept the charge sheet that day. All six accused in the case are currently out on bail.”

However, a check with the general registration (GR) section of the police station on 1 November found that the charge sheet had not yet been submitted to the court.

Money demanded by threatening arrest

According to the PBI investigation, on the night of 16 July 2025, several people identifying themselves as coordinators of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement gathered at the Gulshan-2 roundabout after receiving information that Shammi Ahmed was at her Gulshan residence.

Later, at around 2am, Abdur Razzak and Jane Alam Apu went to Gulshan Police Station, informed the police about the matter and asked them to arrange a raid to arrest her.

The police station informed the deputy commissioner of police of the Gulshan Division. Subsequently, a team comprising police officers and the self-proclaimed coordinators went to the house.

Citing information obtained during the investigation and an examination of video footage, the PBI said that in the early hours of 17 July, several police personnel led by Gulshan Police Station SI Arman Ali, along with Abdur Razzak, Jane Alam Apu, Sakadoun Siam, Sadman Sadab, Ibrahim Hossain, Aminul Islam and 10 to 12 others, went to the residence. Identifying themselves as coordinators, they searched different rooms for the former MP.

Failing to find Shammi Ahmed, they prepared a search list at around 6:30am and left the house.

However, shortly after the police left, Abdur Razzak and Jane Alam Apu returned to the residence. According to the PBI investigation records, they branded the complainant an Awami League collaborator and threatened to have him arrested. They demanded Tk 5 million to spare him from arrest.

Intimidated by the threats, the complainant agreed to pay. After receiving Tk 1 million immediately, the accused left, asking him to keep the remaining Tk 4 million ready. The investigation records also mention that investigators obtained video footage of the money being handed over.

Later, at around 10:30pm on 19 July, Abdur Razzak and Jane Alam Apu returned to the residence. They knocked repeatedly on the flat's door, but left when nobody opened it.

The PBI said an examination of call detail records (CDRs) subsequently confirmed their presence at the scene at that time.

Arrested while collecting the remaining money

According to the PBI investigation records, the accused returned to the house at around 5:30pm on 26 July to collect the remaining Tk 4 million.

The complainant was not at home at the time. Mohammad Hannan, a security guard at the residence, informed him over the phone. The complainant immediately alerted Gulshan Police Station.

Police quickly arrived at the scene and detained Abdur Razzak, Sakadoun Siam, Sadman Sadab, Ibrahim Hossain and Aminul Islam, who was a minor. Jane Alam Apu managed to flee. He was subsequently arrested with the assistance of the Detective Branch (DB) of police.

Among the six arrested, Abdur Razzak and Jane Alam Apu gave confessional statements before the court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The investigation records state that both admitted to receiving the money in their statements.

‘I could not resist the temptation of money’

In his statement before the court, Abdur Razzak alias Riyad admitted to receiving the extortion money.

In the statement, he identified himself as the acting convener of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement among students at a private university. He also claimed to have assisted the police on several occasions in arresting people he described as ‘fascist elements’.

According to Riyad's statement, after receiving information that Shammi Ahmed was at her Gulshan residence on the night of 17 July 2025, they went to the police station. A police team subsequently accompanied them to raid the house. Shammi was not found there.

Riyad told the court that while returning from the house, Jane Alam Apu had brought an AirPod device with him. The device had the words ‘Shammi AirPod’ written on it. They returned to the house at around 10am to hand it back.

Apu entered the house on the pretext of drinking water. They then told the complainant that they knew his wife was inside the house and that they would hand her over to the police.

When the complainant agreed to pay, they initially demanded Tk 5 million. The complainant offered Tk 1 million, which they accepted. They later took the money to Riyad's house and divided it equally among themselves.

Regarding the attempt to collect the remaining Tk 4 million, Riyad said he sent Ibrahim Hossain, Sakadoun Siam and Sadman Sadab to the house at around 5pm on 26 July.

According to him, the police asked him to go to the house as part of a plan to trap him. He was then at the roundabout. Believing what the police told him, he went to the scene. The complainant alerted the police, who arrived and caught them red-handed.

At the end of his statement, Riyad said, “I am a poor man's son. I could not resist the temptation of money. I apologise.”

Apu bought a motorcycle with the extortion money

The investigation records state that accused Jane Alam Apu also admitted to receiving the money in his statement before the court. However, he claimed that he was not present at the scene when the accused demanded the remaining Tk 4 million.

The PBI, however, said Apu was present at the scene but fled.

According to Apu's statement, he had previously served as a coordinator of a committee. On the night of 17 July, after receiving information in a WhatsApp group that a former female MP was at a residence in Gulshan, he went there. A police team subsequently accompanied them to raid the house. The former MP was not found during the raid.

Apu said, “After that, Riyad took me to the house again. When we demanded money from the complainant, he initially agreed to pay Tk 500,000. But Riyad demanded Tk 10 million. After lengthy negotiations, the amount was settled at Tk 5 million. He then gave us Tk 1 million.”

According to Apu, they took the money to Riyad's house in Badda and divided it equally, receiving Tk 500,000 each.

He said he spent Tk 307,000 from his share to buy a Yamaha FZ-X motorcycle and used some of the money to repay debts. He also claimed that an attempt to send another Tk 50,000 through bKash went to the wrong number.

Later, Tk 17,000 was recovered from him.

Apu claimed that when Riyad called him to collect the remaining Tk 4 million, he refused to go. He subsequently cut off contact with Riyad.

He maintained that although Riyad later went to the house with others to demand the money, he was not there and had not exerted any pressure on the former female MP.

Motorcycle and iPhones seized

According to the investigation records, Tk 298,000 and two mobile phones were seized from a house in the Baitakali area of East Badda, identified by Abdur Razzak. The seized phones included a Redmi Note 10 Pro and two iPhone 13 devices.

Meanwhile, acting on information provided by Jane Alam Apu, police seized a Yamaha FZ-X motorcycle, an iPhone 11 and Tk 17,000 in cash from a garage at a house in the Nabinagar area of Mohammadpur.

Akram Hossain, lawyer for the main accused in the case, Abdur Razzak Riyad, told Prothom Alo, “We have not seen the charge sheet yet. We will file a petition in court on behalf of Riyad.”

Attempts to contact Abdur Razzak Riyad, the main accused who is currently out on bail, for his comments on the charge sheet were unsuccessful.

When his phone number was contacted, it was found that his elder brother, Rezaul Karim, was now using it. Riyad's elder brother, Mohammad Rezaul Karim, said Riyad did not wish to comment on the case at this stage.

Expectation of maximum punishment

Muhammad Shamsuddoha Sumon, additional public prosecutor at the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court, told Prothom Alo that Abdur Razzak Riyad, who introduced himself as a leader of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement, was the mastermind behind the extortion.

“He was remanded by the court several times during that period. Everyone accused in the extortion case has been included in the charge sheet. They will face trial in accordance with the charges, and we will seek the maximum punishment for them,” he said.

Zahurul Alam, lawyer for the complainant Siddiq Abu Zafar, told Prothom Alo that he was satisfied that the investigating officer had submitted the charge sheet under the relevant legal provisions. He said they wanted justice.

item.title: Home Ministry asked to take control of properties owned by Sheikh Hasina, Asaduzzaman
item.description:
The Chief Prosecutor's Office has sent a letter to the Ministry of Home Affairs to take control of all movable and immovable properties of the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan, who have been convicted of crimes against humanity.

Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam confirmed to Prothom Alo that the letter was sent today, Tuesday.

The Registrar of the International Crimes Tribunal, the Personal Secretary to the Home Minister, and the Personal Secretary to the Law Minister have been informed about the letter signed by the Chief Prosecutor.

The subject of the letter relates to the implementation of the order to confiscate the properties of the fugitive convicts Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan, who were sentenced by the International Crimes Tribunal-1.

According to the letter, on 17 November 2025, Tribunal-1 sentenced Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan to death for crimes against humanity.

The order was given to seize all properties of the two convicts to distribute compensation to the families of the martyrs and victims of the July uprising.

The tribunal instructed the Ministry of Home Affairs to take necessary measures to implement the property seizure order.

The letter from the Chief Prosecutor's Office further states that if the government does not immediately take control of all movable and immovable properties of the convicted fugitives Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan, they may dispose of, sell, or otherwise transfer the properties at any time, rendering the tribunal's confiscation-related verdict and order ineffective.

In such a situation, it is urgently requested to prepare a complete list of all movable and immovable properties of Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan, take control of them by the state, and distribute them as compensation to the families of the martyrs and victims of the July uprising as per the tribunal's order.

What assets does Sheikh Hasina have?

As candidates in the 2024 twelfth national parliamentary election, Sheikh Hasina (Gopalganj-3) and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal (Dhaka-12) submitted affidavits. From these, their declared asset information can be known.
In the affidavit, Awami League President Sheikh Hasina reported immovable and movable assets valued at Tk 43.4 million under her name.

At that time, she showed cash of Tk 28,500. The amount deposited in banks and financial institutions was about Tk 23.9 million. There were savings certificates worth Tk 2.5 million and fixed deposits (FDR) worth Tk 5.5 million.

Sheikh Hasina declared three motor vehicles in the affidavit, one of which was a gift. She did not declare its value. The remaining two were valued at Tk 4.7 million. Gold and other precious metals were valued at Tk 1. 325 million. She declared the value of her furniture at Tk 740,000.

Sheikh Hasina declared 15. 3 bighas of agricultural land in her name, with a purchased portion valued at Tk 678,000, located in Tungipara, Gopalganj Sadar, Gazipur, and Rangpur.

There is a family farmhouse of Sheikh Hasina and her family located in Telirchala, Mouja, 13 kilometers from Gazipur city, adjacent to the Dhaka-Tangail highway, near the Bangladesh Scout Training Centre.

According to local land office sources, around 1970, a local individual had written this land in the name of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

Sheikh Hasina and Sheikh Rehana inherited ownership of the land. Later, Sheikh Hasina and Sheikh Rehana transferred parts of the land to their children. Consequently, Sheikh Hasina's children Sajib Wazed and Saima Wazed and Sheikh Rehana's children Radwan Mujib Siddiq and Azmina Siddiq became owners. Documents show the land amounting to 297 decimal (9 bighas).

According to the affidavit, Sheikh Hasina has a plot in Purbachal, Dhaka, valued at Tk 3.476 million.

While serving as Prime Minister, Sheikh Hasina, her son Sajib Wazed, daughter Saima Wazed, younger sister Sheikh Rehana (Rehana Siddiq), Rehana's son Radwan Mujib Siddiq, and daughter Azmina Siddiq (Rooponti) were each allotted 10 kathas of land in Purbachal.

In total, the six family members received 60 kathas of land. Allegations of abuse of power and irregularities in these allocations led to ongoing cases by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC).

In the affidavit, Sheikh Hasina showed a three-story building with 6.10 decimals (partially) of land in her name. This land is in Tungipara, Gopalganj. The value during acquisition is shown as Tk 500,000.

On 22 May of last year, the ACC stated in a briefing that Sheikh Hasina had provided false information on her asset disclosure affidavit during the 2008 ninth national parliamentary elections. At the time, she declared having 6.50 acres of land in her name. The purchase price was shown as Tk 175,000.

The ACC revealed that upon verification at the time, Sheikh Hasina had more than 28.41 acres of immovable property in her name. Consequently, the ACC sent a letter to the Election Commission to address the issue.

According to land office sources, the ownership of the house at Dhanmondi 32 belongs to the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Trust.

Sheikh Hasina's residence, Sudha Sadan, in Dhanmondi, belongs to Sajib Wazed and Saima Wazed.

Asaduzzaman Khan's assets

Former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan participated in elections from Dhaka-12 constituency and became a member of parliament. The affidavit he submitted for the twelfth national parliamentary election provides information on declared immovable and movable properties.

Asaduzzaman Khan declared having more than Tk 8.4 million in cash. He showed Tk 8.2 million in bank and financial institution deposits. There were bonds and shares worth about Tk 2.4 million. Postal savings certificates or fixed deposits were shown at Tk 20.1 million.

Asaduzzaman Khan valued two motor vehicles at Tk 16.1 million. His electronic equipment and furniture were valued at Tk 200,000.

He showed a business capital loan of Tk 22 million. He declared 10 tolas of gold, though the price was not mentioned.

According to the affidavit, Asaduzzaman Khan has 171 decimals (over 5 bighas) of agricultural land, valued at Tk 10. 6 million at acquisition.

He has 18. 5 decimals of non-agricultural land, valued at Tk 5.8 million at acquisition. He declared the value of two properties in house and apartment columns. One is noted as a village house, valued at Tk 8 million at acquisition. The other was valued at around Tk 1. 3 million.

Altogether, Asaduzzaman Khan's assets are valued at approximately Tk 102. 5 million (excluding the value of 10 tolas of gold).

The ACC is also investigating Asaduzzaman Khan's assets.

ACC officials have stated that he owns assets beyond known income. The ACC has filed a case in this regard. It was stated in court that he acquired and possessed ownership of asset-value inconsistencies amounting to Tk 164. 2 million through dishonest means.

item.title: Garment workers’ wage board: No step to call meeting in 3 days
item.description:
The government formed a minimum wage board last Sunday to increase wages for workers in the ready-made garment (RMG) industry.

Two days have already passed, but no initiative has been taken to arrange the first meeting of the wage board.

Meanwhile, protests and clashes between workers and police continued today, Tuesday, in Gazipur, Savar-Ashulia and Mirpur.

The Ministry of Labour reconstituted the minimum wage board through a notification on Sunday.

Dhaka University Professor Mosleh Uddin Ahmed was appointed as the independent member of the board, while Asif Ayub, joint secretary general of the Bangladesh Employers' Federation, and Anwar Hossain, president of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, were appointed as the permanent members representing the owners and workers, respectively.

Another gazette was issued on the same day, appointing ABM Shamsuddin, a director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), as the representative of the owners and Babul Akhtar, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Industrial Workers Federation (BGIWF), as the representative of the workers on the minimum wage board formed for the RMG industry.

The six-member wage board will work for the RMG industry with Senior District and Sessions Judge Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman as its chairman.

Asked when the first meeting of the wage board would be held, its chairman, Senior District and Sessions Judge Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, told Prothom Alo on Tuesday afternoon, “We will hold a meeting of the wage board soon. We are ready to hold the meeting.”

Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman said the first meeting of the previous wage board was held 45 days after the notification was issued. The entire process was completed in six to seven months. This time, however, it would not be the same. The government is sincere about completing the process of determining wages within a short time.

The two representatives of the workers on the wage board, Anwar Hossain and Babul Akhtar, held a press conference at the Shram Bhaban yesterday, Monday, urging that a meeting of the wage board be called as soon as possible. They said they would write to the board chairman in this regard.

At the press conference, Babul Akhtar said, “The latest minimum wage structure came into effect in December 2023. Accordingly, a new wage structure is due next December. We will work in such a way that workers receive their wages in January. There is no reason for any delay on our part. If necessary, we will hold meetings of the wage board consecutively. We have no objection to holding meetings throughout the night. We will make no compromise in ensuring workers' rightful wages.”

The last minimum wage board for the RMG industry was formed in 2023. The wage structure was legally required to come into effect on 1 December that year. On 9 April, the Ministry of Labour appointed representatives of the owners and workers to the wage board. The board held six meetings and recommended a minimum wage of Tk 12,500 in the first week of November. The government issued the final notification in December.

The government first formed a minimum wage board for RMG workers in 1994. That board set the minimum wage at Tk 930. In 2006, it was increased to Tk 1,662.50. The 2010 wage board set the minimum wage for workers at Tk 3,000. The 2013 wage board determined the minimum wage at Tk 5,300. The 2018 wage board finalised the minimum wage for garment workers at Tk 8,000.

item.title: Dwip tactfully avoids questions, police seek fresh remand
item.description:
In the murder case of former Bangladesh Air Force Flight Lieutenant KM Tahsif Sauri, the police want to take Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dwip, referred to as a ''younger brother-like friend'', into remand for questioning for the second time.

A seven-day remand request has been made for this purpose.

In the application for the second remand of Dwip, the investigation officer of the case stated that during the first round of remand questioning, the accused provided some important information about the incident.

These pieces of information are being verified. The accused is of a very cunning nature, and hence he tactfully avoids answering multiple questions during interrogation and maintains silence. To question him intensively, it is necessary to take him back into remand.

Tahsif murder case: ‘Younger friend’ Dwip placed on 4-day remand

The investigation officer of the case, Inspector Firoz Uddin of the Naval Police’s Tongi Outpost, applied for this remand in the Dhaka court today, Tuesday.

Public prosecutor Shamsuddoha Sumon confirmed this information to Prothom Alo.

Shamsuddoha Sumon mentioned that the hearing on this remand application is supposed to occur today, Tuesday in the court of Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Hasan Shahadat.

Following his arrest in the case, Dwip was taken into custody for a four-day remand last Saturday for questioning. Today, the Naval Police again applied for his remand for further questioning. In the same case, a young woman, who has also been arrested, is under a four-day remand. Her remand was granted last Sunday.

Ex-Air Force officer’s body recovered from Turag River

On the evening of 27 October, Tahsif went missing after leaving home following Dwip's call. The next afternoon, his body was recovered by the Naval Police from the area of Rajabari Ghat on the Turag River.

In connection with Tahsif's death, his father KM Enayetul Karim filed a murder case last Friday night at the Uttar Khan Police Station in the capital, naming unidentified individuals as the accused.
